root_cause.text: Bluetooth MGMT completion handlers in net/bluetooth/mgmt.c were not updated after mgmt_pending_valid() changed to unlink valid pending commands, causing stale assumptions about pending-list membership that led to double removal in mgmt_add_adv_patterns_monitor_complete() and freeing unrelated concurrent commands via mgmt_pending_foreach() in set_mesh_complete().
root_cause.evidence: The commit message and diff explicitly state that mgmt_pending_valid() “not only validates the pending command but also unlinks it from the pending list,” that calling mgmt_pending_remove() afterward caused a “double list_del()” and list corruption, and that set_mesh_complete()’s mgmt_pending_foreach() could “incorrectly target other pending mesh commands, potentially freeing them while they are still being processed concurrently (leading to UAFs).”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix mesh command error completion to report status for the actual command opcode without broadcasting duplicate responses to other pending commands.
intent_record.what: In the error path of set_mesh_complete(), the code replaces a hardcoded mgmt_cmd_status() call using MGMT_OP_SET_MESH_RECEIVER and removes the subsequent mgmt_pending_foreach(..., cmd_status_rsp, &status) call, instead calling mgmt_cmd_status(cmd->sk, hdev->id, cmd->opcode, status) once.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when status is non-zero, the completion handler now reports the failure only for the actual pending command opcode stored in cmd->opcode rather than always using MGMT_OP_SET_MESH_RECEIVER, and it no longer walks other pending matching management commands to send additional status responses. This prevents misreporting the failed operation and avoids sending extra error notifications to unrelated or additional pending commands.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the correct completion cleanup path by freeing the pending management command instead of removing it after add monitor completion.
intent_record.what: The call to mgmt_pending_remove(cmd) was replaced with mgmt_pending_free(cmd) in mgmt_add_adv_patterns_monitor_complete() after mgmt_cmd_complete() is invoked.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this changes the cleanup behavior for the pending management command from removing it via the pending-command removal path to directly freeing it, ensuring the command object is released using the appropriate completion-time cleanup routine and avoiding incorrect pending-list handling or resource management.

grouping_result.intent: Fix mesh command error completion to report status for the actual command opcode without broadcasting duplicate responses to other pending commands.
Use the correct completion cleanup path by freeing the pending management command instead of removing it after add monitor completion.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly targets set_mesh_complete() behavior after pending-command handling changed: it stops iterating/broadcasting to other pending commands and instead completes only the actual mesh command opcode, which matches the root cause involving mgmt_pending_foreach() incorrectly affecting unrelated concurrent commands.

The change directly fixes one of the root-cause manifestations: after mgmt_pending_valid() began unlinking valid pending commands, the completion handler could no longer assume the command was still on the pending list. Switching add monitor completion from removing to freeing the pending command addresses that stale assumption and prevents the double-removal bug.

candidates.rationale: After mgmt_pending_valid() began unlinking the validated pending command, iterating over all pending commands of this opcode and freeing them via the callback could affect unrelated concurrent commands. This is the direct stale-membership assumption behind the set_mesh_complete vulnerability.

The completion handler assumed the command was still linked on the pending list, but mgmt_pending_valid() had already unlinked valid commands. Calling mgmt_pending_remove(cmd) again therefore caused a double removal / invalid cleanup in mgmt_add_adv_patterns_monitor_complete().

vuln_statements.explanation: This completion handler performed removal assuming the validated pending command was still linked in the pending list. After mgmt_pending_valid() changed to unlink valid commands, this statement attempted a second removal of the same command, causing the double-removal bug in mgmt_add_adv_patterns_monitor_complete().

This iterated over all pending commands for the opcode and, via its callback path, could free unrelated concurrent commands. That behavior relied on the stale assumption that the just-validated command was still on the pending list after mgmt_pending_valid(), leading set_mesh_complete() to affect other pending operations incorrectly.

    ==================================================================

bic_trace_step.reason:
The snippet is sufficient because it shows the exact completion handlers and pending-list iteration logic relevant to the stated root cause. The vulnerable construct is still present in both places named in the root cause.

1) In `set_mesh_complete`, the code still does `mgmt_pending_foreach(MGMT_OP_SET_MESH_RECEIVER, hdev, true, cmd_status_rsp, &status);` in the error path. The callback `cmd_status_rsp` was changed to only call `mgmt_cmd_status(cmd->sk, cmd->hdev->id, cmd->opcode, *status);` and no longer removes the command (`mgmt_pending_remove(cmd)` was deleted). With `mgmt_pending_foreach(..., true, ...)`, the foreach helper is expected to unlink valid pending commands itself, matching the root-cause description that `mgmt_pending_valid()` now unlinks entries. Iterating all matching pending commands in `set_mesh_complete` therefore still risks acting on and unlinking unrelated concurrent commands of the same opcode, which is exactly the vulnerability described.

2) In `mgmt_add_adv_patterns_monitor_complete`, the code still ends with `mgmt_cmd_complete(...); mgmt_pending_remove(cmd);`. Since the root cause states that after the helper change valid pending commands may already be unlinked before completion handlers run, this completion handler still assumes the command is on the pending list and performs an explicit removal. That stale assumption is the double-removal pattern called out in the root cause.

The commit mainly adds locking/iteration-mode plumbing (`mgmt_pending_foreach(..., true/false, ...)`) and removes some direct frees/removes in generic callbacks, but it does not show the semantic fix for these two vulnerable cases. In particular, `mgmt_add_adv_patterns_monitor_complete` still explicitly removes `cmd`, and `set_mesh_complete` still bulk-iterates `MGMT_OP_SET_MESH_RECEIVER` pending commands with removal-enabled foreach behavior. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is not yet fully in place.
